scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You touch your thumb to the phone, and it unlocks in a blink. But how does it know it's you?

scenes.name: ridges
scenes.text: Your fingertip is covered in ridges and valleys. The pattern is unique, even between identical twins.

scenes.name: scan
scenes.text: The sensor reads that pattern. Many phones use tiny capacitor cells. Others, under the screen, use light or sound to image it.

scenes.name: points
scenes.text: Software doesn't keep the photo. It finds key points, where ridges end or split, and maps their positions and angles.

scenes.name: enroll
scenes.text: When you set it up, several touches build a template. It's stored in a locked area of the chip that apps can't read.

scenes.name: match
scenes.text: Each new touch is turned into points and compared with that template. Enough matching points gives a high score.

scenes.name: unlock
scenes.text: Above the threshold, the secure chip says yes, and the phone unlocks. A stranger's finger fools it roughly once in fifty thousand tries.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Ridges, points, template, score. All in a split second. Follow for more on how things really work.
